words.desc: A winged unicorn with a single spiraling horn, a magical beast of fantasy and legend.
A legendary two-headed creature from myth that rolls its body like a wheel across the ground.
A winged spirit who carries messages between divine and earthly realms.
A legendary serpent king whose deadly gaze can kill with a single look.
A large hairy ape-like creature said to live in North American forests.
A mythical creature with a human upper body joined to the body of a horse.
The three-headed dog that guards the gates of the Greek underworld.
A fire-breathing monster made of parts of a lion, a goat and a serpent.
A legendary two-legged dragon with a rooster's head, hatched from a cockerel's egg.
A huge brute from Greek myth with one eye in the middle of its forehead.
A huge winged reptile of legend that breathes flames and guards treasure.
A tree spirit from ancient myth who watches the forest.
A short, sturdy and bearded being of legend famed for mining and metalwork.
A magical humanlike being of folklore known for keen senses and a long life.
A tiny magical winged being, often helpful, found in many children's stories.
A gentle Roman woodland spirit with a human upper body and the legs and horns of a goat.
A supernatural being from Middle Eastern tales who grants wishes.
The spirit of a dead person believed to appear to the living.
A small bearded earth spirit of folklore, often shown wearing a pointed red hat.
A small ugly creature from folklore known for being sly, greedy and mischievous.
An animated figure from Jewish folklore made from clay or mud.
A monstrous woman of Greek myth with living snakes for hair and a petrifying gaze.
A legendary beast with the head and wings of an eagle and a lion's body.
A creature of Greek myth with a woman's face and the body of a bird.
A many-headed serpent monster that grows new heads whenever one is cut off.
A shape-shifting water horse from Scottish folklore.
A gigantic many-armed monster of Scandinavian legend that drags ships underwater.
A small bearded Irish sprite who mends shoes and guards hidden treasure.
A man-eating beast of Persian legend with a lion's build, a person's face and a stinging tail.
A legendary ocean dweller with the upper body of a woman and the tail of a fish.
A monster from Greek myth with the head of a bull and the body of a man.
An ancient corpse preserved by embalming and wrapped in long strips of cloth.
A beautiful minor nature goddess of Greek myth who lives in trees, rivers or mountains.
A huge ugly brute from folk tales that likes to eat people.
The winged white stallion of ancient legend that sprang from a slain gorgon's neck.
A legendary bird that bursts into flames and is born again from the ashes.
A tiny mischievous being of English West Country folklore, said to lead travellers astray.
A woodland nature spirit of Greek myth, part man and part goat, fond of revelry.
A seal-folk from Celtic lore who sheds its skin to become human.
A dangerous creature of Greek myth whose beautiful singing lured seamen to their deaths.
A creature with a lion's body and a human head that poses riddles to travellers.
A large ugly creature of Scandinavian folklore that lurks under bridges or in mountains.
A legendary white horse with a single spiral horn on its forehead.
An undead being of folklore that rises at night to drink human blood.
A person cursed to turn into a fierce wolf whenever the moon is full.
A winged reptile of legend with two legs instead of four and a venomous tail.
A huge ape-like creature said to roam the snowy mountains of Asia.
A dead body brought back to life that shuffles around hungry for flesh.
